assessment: The authors report that neurons in V1 and V4 multiplex information of simultaneously presented objects. A combination of multi-single unit recordings, statistical modelling of neuronal responses and neuronal correlations analyses argues in favor of their claims. Pairs of neurons having similar object preferences tended to be positively correlated when both objects were presented, while pairs of neurons having different object preferences tended to be negatively correlated and these patterns and others suggest that information about the two objects is multiplexed in time. These results are of broad interest to the field, as they shed new light on the "binding" problem and highlight the importance of underexplored features of cortical activity for neural coding.
